_README: Function/tool descriptions handed to T1 so it can select a CALL SEQUENCE, not just skill names.
This file is an OVERLAY on skills.yaml, not a replacement. skills.yaml stays the single source
of skill IDENTITY -- the names here must already exist there, and the loader refuses to start if
one does not (a typo would otherwise silently produce a function the model can name but the
registry cannot route). Skills absent from this file still render from skills.yaml as before, so
adding an entry here is additive and never drops a skill.
What this file adds over skills.yaml: a call-style `description` and `completion_cue`.
Edit freely -- it is read at orchestrator startup, no code change needed. Keep `name` in sync with
skills.yaml; everything else is prose for the model.

functions.name: crawl_through
functions.description: VISUAL TEST: you LOOK DOWN onto the tabletop -- its top surface is clearly visible from above, i.e. the table is lower than the camera. FALLBACK ONLY: crawl THROUGH the gap beneath an obstacle that is TOO LOW TO CROUCH UNDER -- its underside is clearly below the robot's chest, around waist height or lower (low desk, coffee table, low bar or beam), so it needs hands-and-knees. For any table the robot can clear by bending its knees on its feet (underside at or above chest height: tall desk, standing desk, bar, high table) use crouch_under instead -- crouch is the default, never crawl under a high table. Handles the full traversal: enter on one side, emerge on the far side. Completion is confirmed only when the obstacle is fully behind the robot and open space is ahead.
functions.completion_cue: Obstacle is fully behind the robot; open space is visible ahead. Robot is NOT still beneath the obstacle.

functions.name: sit
functions.description: Approach a seat or chair that is directly visible ahead with a clear, unobstructed path, and sit down. Do NOT invoke if a low obstacle lies between the robot and the seat — resolve the obstacle first (e.g. crawl_through).
functions.completion_cue: Judge from mission context and current ego view; no fixed visual cue documented.
